label: conj:poincare-lefschetz-borromean
title: Poincaré–Lefschetz duality on Borromean complement — cohomology ↔ homology of manifold-with-cusps
html:
The Borromean complement \mathbf{S}^3 \setminus \mathcal{B}_3 is a 3-manifold with cusps (boundary = 3 disjoint tori). Poincaré–Lefschetz duality gives a canonical isomorphism:

  H^k(\mathbf{S}^3 \setminus \mathcal{B}_3, \partial) \;\cong\;
  H_{3-k}(\mathbf{S}^3 \setminus \mathcal{B}_3),

relating cohomology with boundary support to homology. In particular H^2(\partial \mathcal{B}_3) \cong H_1(\mathbf{S}^3 \setminus \mathcal{B}_3) \cong \mathbb{Z}^3 (the three meridian classes around the three Borromean components). The duality pairs the volume form (top cohomology) with the fundamental class (top homology), giving the natural categorical home for \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = 8G as a Poincaré–Lefschetz pairing.

Relationship to the Bloch-group route

The K-theoretic Bloch-group element (Borromean rings represent a non-trivial element of K_3(\mathbb{C}) / Bloch group with regulator r_2 = 8G) provides the regulator side of the Borromean structure (r_2[\mathcal{B}_3] = 8G). Poincaré–Lefschetz provides the topological side: the volume form \in H^3 pairs with the fundamental class \in H_3 to give the volume integral 8G.

The two are the same number (8G = \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)), but expressed through distinct dualities: Poincaré–Lefschetz is the topological-cohomological route, the Bloch group the K-theoretic one.

Structural invariants

  • GB filtration: N/A — manifold-with-boundary duality is at the topological level, not at the Hecke-element level.
  • Jet order: h^0 — Poincaré–Lefschetz acts on the leading- order topological volume.
  • Bar-symmetry: bar-symmetric (the duality is independent of q-parameter; both sides are classical-topology constructions).

What remains open

  1. Verify that the Borromean volume 8G arises as a Poincaré– Lefschetz pairing.
  2. Connect to the Bloch-group route: show the regulator r_2 and the Poincaré–Lefschetz pairing both produce 8G via the vol-as-motivic-period framing.
  3. Closing the conjecture needs Poincaré–Lefschetz duality for manifolds with cusps, in the form used above.
